records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, what minimum duration defines Inpatient Hospitalisation on Page 1, and what daily room rent limit applies on Page 2?
records.answer:
In Apex Health Shield Version 2, **Inpatient Hospitalisation** is defined as an admission into a hospital for a minimum contiguous period of **24 consecutive hours** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1].  

The daily room rent limit applicable under this version is **Rs. 7,500 per day** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2].

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, how does the Pre-existing Disease definition time window on Page 1 correspond to the PED waiting period on Page 3?
records.answer:
The definition of a Pre‑existing Disease (PED) on Page 1 states that a condition is considered pre‑existing if it was diagnosed, had signs or symptoms, or was treated within **36 months prior to policy inception** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1].  
On Page 3, the waiting period for claims related to a Pre‑existing Disease is also **36 months** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].  

Thus, the time window used to define a PED matches exactly the waiting period that must elapse before such a condition can be covered under the policy.

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, how is Co-payment defined on Page 1, and what specific percentage applies to senior citizens on Page 6?
records.answer:
Co‑payment is defined on Page 1 as a cost‑sharing requirement under the policy that requires the policyholder to bear a specified percentage of the admissible claim amount [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1].  
On Page 6, the policy states that the mandatory co‑payment for insured persons aged 65 years and above is reduced to **10 %** per admissible claim [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.6].

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, what is the initial waiting period for day care procedures on Page 2 compared to the general initial waiting period on Page 3?
records.answer:
The initial waiting period for day‑care procedures is **30 days** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2].  
The general initial waiting period for all illnesses (except accidental bodily injury) is also **30 days** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, how does the organ donor limit in the benefits table on Page 2 align with the organ donor support clause on Page 6?
records.answer:
The benefits table on Page 2 states that organ‑donor expenses are covered up to **Rs. 2,00,000 per policy year** (with a 12‑month period) [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2].  
The organ‑donor support clause on Page 6 confirms that hospitalisation expenses for organ donation harvesting from a living donor are payable up to an **enhanced limit of Rs. 2,00,000** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.6].  

Thus, the two provisions are aligned: both set the same maximum coverage amount of Rs. 2,00,000 for organ‑donor related expenses.

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, what is the cataract surgery waiting period in the table on Page 3, and what sub-limit is specified in Clause 3.4 on Page 3 and Page 2?
In Apex Health Shield Version 2, how does the accidental bodily injury exception to the waiting period on Page 3 relate to the reconstructive cosmetic surgery clause on Page 4?
records.answer:
The waiting‑period table on page 3 specifies a 30‑day waiting period for “All illnesses except accidental bodily injury” [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3]. This wording means that accidental bodily injury is not subject to that 30‑day waiting period (i.e., it either has no waiting period or a different one not listed).  

On page 4 the policy states that cosmetic surgery is excluded unless it is “required reconstructive surgery following accidental bodily injury” [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4]. Thus, accidental bodily injury is the only circumstance under which reconstructive cosmetic surgery is covered, and it is also the only circumstance where the 30‑day waiting period does not apply.

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, what is the maternity benefit waiting period under Section 4.3 on Page 4 compared to the general initial waiting period on Page 3?
records.answer:
In Apex Health Shield Version 2, the maternity benefit under Section 4.3 on Page 4 has a waiting period of **24 months** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4].  
By contrast, the general initial waiting period for all illnesses (except accidental bodily injury) listed on Page 3 is **30 days** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, what notice is required for planned admission on Page 5, and what minimum hospital stay is required on Page 1?
records.answer:
The policy requires that for a planned admission the insured (or their representative) must give notice to the insurer **at least 48 hours before the scheduled admission** at a network hospital [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.5].  

It also defines an inpatient hospitalisation as an admission that lasts for a **minimum contiguous period of 24 consecutive hours** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1].

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, what is the Free-Look Period duration defined on Page 1, and what refund terms apply under Section 5.3 on Page 5?
records.answer:
The Free‑Look Period is **15 days** from the date the policyholder receives the policy documents [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1].  

Under Section 5.3 on Page 5, the policy states that if no claim is made during that 15‑day period, the premium is **refunded subject to minimal administrative charges** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.5].

records.question: Do both Version 1 and Version 2 of Apex Health Shield cover maternity expenses, and how do they differ?
records.answer:
Version 1 of the Apex Health Shield policy does **not** cover maternity expenses.  
In Version 1, maternity and childbirth are listed as exclusions under Section 4.3 [APEX_HEALTH_V1 p.4].

Version 2 of the policy **does** cover maternity expenses.  
Section 4.3 of Version 2 states that inpatient medical expenses for maternity and normal or cesarean delivery are covered up to Rs. 50,000 per delivery, after a waiting period of 24 months, and this benefit is available for up to two deliveries [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4].

Thus, the key differences are:  
- Version 1 excludes all maternity and childbirth costs, whereas Version 2 provides coverage for up to two deliveries.  
- Version 2 includes a specific monetary limit (Rs. 50,000 per delivery) and a 24‑month waiting period, which are not present in Version 1.
